{{short description|Austronesian language spoken in the Philippines}} {{use dmy dates|date=July 2024}} {{Infobox language |name=Arta |states=[[Philippines]] |region=northern [[Luzon]] |ethnicity=150 (no date){{e16|atz|Arta}} |speakers=11 |date=2013 |ref=e18 |familycolor=Austronesian |fam2=[[Malayo-Polynesian languages|Malayo-Polynesian]] |fam3=[[Philippine languages|Philippine]]? |fam4=[[Northern Luzon languages|Northern Luzon]] |iso3=atz |glotto=arta1239 |glottorefname=Arta }} '''Arta''' is a highly endangered [[Philippine Negrito languages|Negrito language]] of the northern [[Philippines]].{{Glottolog|arta1239|Arta}} ==Distribution== Lawrence Reid's 1990 fieldwork revealed only 12 speakers in Villa Santiago, [[Aglipay, Quirino|Aglipay]], [[Quirino]] Province,{{cite journal |last=Reid |first=Lawrence A. |date=Summer 1989 |jstor=3622974 |title=Arta, Another Philippine Negrito Language |journal=Oceanic Linguistics |volume=28 |issue=1 |pages=47–74|doi=10.2307/3622974 |hdl=10125/32983 |hdl-access=free }} and in 1992 it was spoken by only three families. It is not closely related to other languages. There are still small groups of Arta speakers in [[Maddela, Quirino|Maddela]] and [[Nagtipunan, Quirino|Nagtipunan]] towns of [[Quirino Province]].{{sfn|Lobel|2013|p=88}} Kimoto (2017) reports that Arta has 10 native speakers and 35–45 second-language speakers living primarily in Pulang Lupa, Kalbo, and in Dissimungal, Nagtipunan.{{sfn|Kimoto|2017}} The Arta are found in the following places within [[Nagtipunan, Quirino|Nagtipunan]] Municipality.{{cite report |last=Kimoto |first=Yukinori |url=https://www.academia.edu/6076816 |title=A preliminary report on the grammar of Arta}} *Nagtipunan Municipality **Dissimungal Barangay ***Purok Kalbo ***Pulang Lupa ***Tilitilan **San Ramos Barangay **Pongo Barangay **Sangbay Barangay Arta is in contact with [[Casiguran Agta language|Casiguran Agta]], [[Nagtipunan Agta language|Nagtipunan Agta]], [[Yogad language|Yogad]], Ilokano, and Tagalog.{{sfn|Kimoto|2017}} ==Phonology== Arta is notable for having [[vowel length]] distinction, an unusual typological feature in the Philippines.{{sfn|Kimoto|2017}} ==Sound changes== Kimoto (2017) lists the following [[sound change]]s from [[Proto-Malayo-Polynesian language|Proto-Malayo-Polynesian]] (PMP) to Arta. Long vowels in Arta are derived from PMP diphthongs.{{sfn|Kimoto|2017|pp=56-67}} {| class="wikitable sortable" ! [[Proto-Malayo-Polynesian language|PMP]] !!
